cells.tense: The pattern is landing now and your hand is already on the pen.
cells.ask: Write the first new pattern you noticed today on one page, then show it to one person it touches.
cells.core:
Something is arriving and you are seeing it for what it is. The mind is running at full width, sharp enough to catch what usually stays blurred. No hunting for a pattern to justify anything, no second-guessing whether you really saw it.

One thing is harder. What you catch arrives before anyone has felt it with you. That is where the pull to hold the possible feelings comes in — to carry what others might feel alongside what you have seen. Bring one more piece of that catching into the room where people are, rather than keeping it in the mind alone. Held too long before it is shared, it starts carrying you less than you carry it.
cells.sheetLine: You are catching it clearly, and the clarity reaches one person at a time.
cells.verb: catching the shape of what is arriving
cells.place: at the doorway where what is coming in first shows itself

cells.tense: You are already standing where this has been worked out and nothing is left unclear.
cells.ask: Put the framework away for one day and note what stays unclear — that is the appointment you are keeping.
cells.core:
You are ahead of the arrival. The pattern is being applied before it fully lands — explanations forming early, the next two moves already mapped, everyone around already caught up to where you are. The catching is real and the timing has jumped a step past what has actually come in.

Going well, this looks like letting a thing finish showing you what it is before you name it. What this needs is something solid to organize by, structure that serves what it holds and stays loose enough that new feeling still gets in. At the moment the analysis is closing early. Let one piece of what comes in stay undecided through an evening, and the sharpness stops cutting the thing it was meant to open.
cells.sheetLine: You are explaining it before it finishes arriving.

cells.tense: The catching happened once, near a doorway you stopped short of, and you have stood there since.
cells.ask: Write down one pattern you already trust, in words someone else could use, and take it to the person it fits.
cells.core:
The sense that something is coming in has gone quiet. Not because nothing is arriving — the doorway is still where it was — but because the last time something landed, what followed did not go well, and the catching went still after that. Holding a piece back is understandable.

Going well, this looks like carrying what you already see out where someone else is, and letting their response do half the work. What is missing is company for it: it needs to travel through another person to come back alive for you. Not more looking inward. Carry one piece out in whatever shape it is in now, and what feeds the catching comes back on the return trip.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing is arriving because the last arrival taught you not to look.
cells.verb: catching the shape of what is arriving

cells.tense: You are already putting the pieces together and calling it something that just happens.
cells.ask: Say out loud to one person which new pattern changed how you see this, and name that you are the one who found it.
cells.core:
You are already doing the work — you can feel a pattern fall into place when it comes, a sense of what fits and what will not. The description lags: the putting-together is happening while the estimator stays off the record.

The feelings of others are in the mix too, quietly shaping which patterns you keep to hand. Weighing that is right, and it is not a failure of nerve. Credit where it belongs, though. Say the thing that landed is yours and that you were the one who saw it, and the sharpest of what is entering stops arriving in your name only.
cells.sheetLine: You are already putting it together. You just haven't put your name on it.
